task_instruction:
Persona:

	At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

	Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

	When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

Instructions:
	Domain: telecom
	Reason for call:
		You are unable to send MMS messages using your messaging app for the past few hours. You want to fix it and successfully send an MMS message.
	Known info:
		You are John Smith with phone number 555-123-2002. You are currently abroad in France.
	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You are willing to refuel 2.0 GB of data if necessary, but you do not want to change your mobile data plan. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought: Hi! How can I help you today?
turns.execution_output: User: Hello, dear. I'm having a bit of trouble with my phone. For the past few hours, I haven't been able to send those picture messages — the ones with photos of my grandchildren. It's the regular messaging app I always use. I'm not very good with these things, so I'm hoping you can help me.

turns.thought:
Of course, I'd be happy to help you get picture messaging working again! Before we start, I'll need to look up your account. Could you please give me either:

- **The phone number** on the line that's having trouble, or
- **Your full name and date of birth** (for verification)?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, of course. My name is John Smith, and my phone number is 555-123-2002. I hope that's what you need, dear.

turns.thought:
I've found the likely cause. Your line (555-123-2002) is on the Premium Plan with a 15 GB monthly data limit, and you've used **15.1 GB** this cycle — just over the limit. When a plan's data limit is reached, data connectivity is cut off, and picture messaging (MMS) needs mobile data to send.

The good news is I can add more data to your line right away so you can send those photos again. It's $2.00 per GB on your plan, and I can add up to 2 GB.

How much data would you like me to add — 1 GB ($2.00) or 2 GB ($4.00)?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh dear, I had no idea I'd used all my data. Well, I certainly don't want to change my plan — I like the one I have. But if adding some data will let me send those pictures to my family, then... let's go ahead and add the 2 GB, please. That's the $4.00 one, right? That won't change my plan or anything, will it?

turns.thought: Yes, that's right — 2 GB for $4.00, and it won't change your plan at all. It just adds extra data to your line for this billing cycle. Let me apply that now.
turns.execution_output: {"message": "Successfully added 2 GB of data for line L1002 for $4.00", "new_data_refueling_gb": "2.0", "charge": "4.0"}

turns.thought:
All done! Here's what I did:

- **Added 2 GB of data** to your line 555-123-2002 for **$4.00** (added to your bill — the charge showed as $4.00)
- **Your plan has not changed** — you're still on the Premium Plan at $65.00/month. This is just a one-time data top-up for this billing cycle, which runs through February 28, 2025.

You should now be able to send those pictures of your grandchildren. If your phone is still having trouble, please try turning the phone off and back on, as a restart often helps the new data allowance take effect.

Just so you know: your plan includes 15 GB per month, and you had used 15.1 GB, which is what stopped the picture messages. Now that I've added 2 GB, you have room again for the rest of this cycle. Is there anything else I can help you with?

The data definitely went through — I verified your line now has 2 GB of refueled data. Don't worry, your photos are safe on your phone; nothing has been lost. Since the data top-up didn't fix it, let me keep troubleshooting other possible causes. Let me check a few settings on your line.

I've re-checked your line, and yes — the data did go through properly. The 2 GB top-up is confirmed on line 555-123-2002 (it now shows 2.0 GB of refueled data), so your photos are safe and nothing was lost. Your line is Active, not suspended, and your bill is in good standing.

Since the data is in place, there must be something else on the phone itself preventing picture messages from going through. Would you be able to check a couple of things for me?

1. **Restart your phone.** Sometimes the phone needs a fresh start to pick up the new data allowance. Please turn it completely off, wait about 30 seconds, then turn it back on.
2. **Look at the top of your screen.** Do you see a signal strength icon (the little bars) and a network type such as "5G," "LTE," or "4G"?

Then please try sending a picture message again and let me know what happens.

If it's still not working after the restart, I can walk you through a few more settings on your phone (Smartphone Pro Max) that commonly affect picture messaging — such as your mobile data switch, network mode, and a setting called APN that picture messages rely on. We'll get this sorted out together. Would you like to try the restart first?
turns.execution_output: User: Oh, a restart... that makes me nervous. I have so many photos of my grandchildren on this phone — will turning it off and on again delete any of them? I don't want to lose anything. Are you quite sure it's safe?

turns.thought:
Yes, I completely understand your worry — those photos are precious. I want to reassure you:

**A restart will not delete anything on your phone.** Restarting simply turns the phone's software off and back on again. Your photos, messages, contacts, and apps all stay exactly as they are — they're stored in the phone's memory, which isn't touched by a restart.

The only thing a restart does is give the phone a fresh start so it can recognize changes — in your case, the 2 GB of data I just added to your line. It's comparable to turning a lamp off and back on; the light bulb and everything around it are unaffected.

Of course, I'll never ask you to do anything risky. A restart is one of the simplest and safest things you can do with a phone, and I've already confirmed your data went through properly, so your pictures are perfectly safe.

Would you like to give it a try? Here's how:

1. Press and hold the power button on the side of your phone.
2. When the "slide to power off" (or "Power off") option appears, follow it to turn the phone off.
3. Wait about 30 seconds.
4. Press and hold the power button again until you see the logo, then let go.

Once it's back on, try sending one of those picture messages and let me know how it goes. Take your time — there's no rush.
turns.execution_output: User: Well, alright dear, if you're sure it won't hurt anything. Let me try it... I'm holding the button now.

turns.thought:
Oh, you haven't broken anything at all — I promise! That little airplane symbol is actually great news, because it's very likely the whole reason your picture messages won't send.

That airplane symbol means **Airplane Mode is turned ON**. When it's on, your phone switches off all its wireless connections — cellular service, mobile data, and Wi-Fi. That's why you don't see any signal bars or "4G"/"5G" at the top of your screen. And picture messages need mobile data to send, so they simply can't go through while Airplane Mode is on. It can get switched on quite easily by accident, so please don't worry.

Here's how to turn it off:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** with one finger. This opens a panel of quick settings with round or square icons.
2. Look for the **airplane icon** — it's probably lit up or highlighted (that means it's ON).
3. **Tap that airplane icon once.** It should go dim or grey, which means Airplane Mode is now OFF.
4. Wait a few seconds, then look at the top of your screen again — you should now see the **signal bars** return, along with **"5G," "LTE," or "4G."**

Once you see those bars back, please try sending a picture message again.

Please don't worry about your photos — Airplane Mode doesn't affect anything stored on your phone, and turning it off certainly won't delete anything.

Let me know what you see at the top of your screen once you've done that. If the bars come back and the picture message still won't send, we'll look at the next setting together. You're doing just fine.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try to find that airplane thing... I'm swiping down from the top now. I think I see it. Tapping it...

turns.thought:
It's perfectly okay — you did it right! Turning off Airplane Mode was the correct step, and the airplane symbol being gone confirms it worked. You're doing great.

Now we know a bit more: "No Signal" means your phone isn't connecting to the network, and "Data Disabled" means the mobile data switch is turned off. Let me check a couple of things on your line for you.

You did exactly the right thing — well done! Turning off Airplane Mode was the correct step, and I can see it worked because the airplane symbol is gone.

We're making progress. Now we have two new clues, and both are fixable:

**1. "Data Disabled"** — this means your phone's mobile data switch is turned off. Since picture messages need mobile data, we need to turn this back on.

**2. "No Signal"** — the phone isn't connecting to the network yet. Turning mobile data on often brings the signal bars back, so let's do that first.

Here's what to do, using that same quick settings panel:

1. **Swipe down from the very top of your screen** again, just like you did before.
2. Look for the icon for **mobile data** — it usually looks like a small **up-and-down arrow** pair, and it's often labelled "Mobile data" or "Cellular data." Right now it's probably greyed out or dim because it's off.
3. **Tap that icon once** to turn it on. It should light up or become highlighted.
4. Wait about 10–20 seconds, then look at the top of your screen and tell me what you see.

Please don't be flustered — you're doing really well, and none of this has any effect on your photos. They're all still safely on your phone.

Once you've done that, let me know whether the **signal bars** and **"5G," "LTE," or "4G"** have appeared at the top. If "No Signal" is still showing, I'll guide you through the next step. We'll get this sorted together.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, I'm swiping down again... I see some little arrows. Tapping those...

turns.thought: Let me check a few things on your line and device directly.

I've double-checked your account, and I have good news and a clear next step.

**Your line is perfectly fine.** I verified it just now — line 555-123-2002 is **Active**, not suspended, and your bills are in good standing (your January bill is paid in full). The 2 GB of data I added is confirmed on the line. So the problem is definitely something on the phone itself, not with your service. Nothing is broken, and your photos are completely safe.

You likely tapped the right icon, but it didn't respond. Let's try it a different way, through the phone's main Settings:

1. Find the **Settings** app on your phone (it looks like a **grey gear/cog** icon) and tap it.
2. Tap **"Network & Internet"** — or it may be called **"Connections"** or **"Mobile Network."**
3. Tap **"Mobile network"** or **"Mobile data."**
4. You should see a switch for **"Mobile data."** If it's grey/off, tap it so it turns on (it'll usually slide to the right or turn blue/green).
5. Press the **Home button** or swipe up to go back to your main screen, wait about 20 seconds, and check the top of the screen.

If the data switch is already ON in Settings but the top of the screen still says "Data Disabled," or if you can't get the switch to move, just tell me and I'll try a different approach with you.

**One more important thing about "No Signal":** since turning Airplane Mode off didn't bring the bars back, there's a good chance your SIM card — the small card inside the phone that connects you to the network — needs to be re-seated. I can guide you through that safely, and it doesn't affect your photos at all.

So, please try the Settings steps above first, then tell me:
- Does the top of the screen still say **"Data Disabled"**?
- Do you see any **signal bars** yet?

Take your time, and let me know what you see. We'll get those pictures to your family.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me try that little switch again... I'm tapping it now.
